name: Vercel Sandbox

modes.label: On-demand, iad1 / cle1 / pdx1 (base rate)
modes.note: Active CPU $0.128/vCPU-h (I/O and LLM wait not billed) + provisioned memory $0.0212/GB-h for full session wall-clock incl. idle. Memory fixed 2 GB/vCPU. 1-minute minimum applies to memory per session; Active CPU metering granularity unpublished. Creation fee $0.60/1M Sandbox.create() calls (resume is not a creation). Same unit rates Pro and Enterprise. Basis check 2026-09-28: Active CPU = 'The amount of time your code actively uses the CPU' (I/O wait excluded); memory = 'The memory allocated to your sandbox (in GB) multiplied by the time it runs' (https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing). No idle auto-stop: 'when a session times out, Vercel stops it', but the timeout is wall-clock (default 5 min) and 'A session is billed for the full time it runs, even while idle' (https://vercel.com/kb/guide/vercel-sandbox-duration-and-persistence), so auto_stop_idle stays false. Same basis for all region modes.

modes.label: Region pinned: icn1 (Seoul)
modes.note: Data transfer $0.35/GB (highest of all regions; card network block uses iad1 $0.15).

modes.label: Region pinned: gru1 (Sao Paulo), most expensive
modes.note: Data transfer $0.22/GB; drives $0.0891/GB-mo. 1.73x iad1 on CPU and memory.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Allotment is in units, not dollars: 5 Active-CPU h + 420 GB-h memory + 5,000 creations + 20 GB transfer per month (= ~$12.55 at iad1 rates: 0.64 + 8.904 + 0.003 + 3.00); 15 GB snapshot + 15 GB drive storage lifetime. HARD STOP: no overage; creation paused until 30 days after first use once any quota is exceeded. vCPU allocation 20-40/min. One Hobby team per account; non-commercial. Verifier 2026-09-28: marked trial_only because the engine would bill usage above included_usd as overage, which Hobby cannot incur ('You will not be charged for any additional usage. Once you exceed the quotas, sandbox creation is paused', https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing), and Hobby is non-commercial.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $20 platform fee = $20 monthly usage credit shared across ALL Vercel products (expires monthly), 1 deploying seat included, extra deploying seats $20/mo, viewers free. Sandbox data transfer covered by Flat Rate CDN included tier (1 TB + 1M CDN requests, shared with site CDN traffic); exceeding moves to $20/$100/$300 tiers next cycle. vCPU allocation 150 -> 5,000/min. Spend management soft (alerts; optional pause of production deployments).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom contract / Flexible Commitment prepaid balance. Same published unit rates as Pro but NO Flat Rate CDN bundle for sandbox transfer: $0.15/GB iad1 (up to $0.35/GB icn1). Secure Compute (static egress IPs, VPC peering) Enterprise-only, network fee unpublished, Private Data Transfer $0.15/GB. Higher concurrency via sales; control plane 100k req/min.

perf_source: StarSling hpc-sandbox-benchmarks, run 36498291449 (2026-09-29), Node.js V8 Web Tooling p50 at a 4 vCPU / 8 GB target

knobs.label: Idle time billed until the session timeout (× session hours)
knobs.why: Vercel has no idle auto-stop: provisioned memory bills for the full session wall-clock (idle included) until stop() or the timeout (default 5 min, extendable to the plan max of 24 h Pro/Ent). Active CPU is not billed while idle, so the factor slightly overstates CPU. Default 1 = stop() when work ends; 2x ceiling is a judgment call. Regions are already separate modes, so no region knob.

caveats: Memory is billed on provisioned size for the whole session wall-clock (idle included); only CPU is active-billed. There is no idle auto-stop: sessions run until the timeout (default 5 min, extendable to plan max) or stop().

Regional rates taken from the regionalPricing data embedded in the pricing page (fetched 2026-09-28); per-region data-transfer and drive rates also differ, but the card network block uses iad1 ($0.15/GB).
Hobby included_usd (12.55) is a dollar-equivalent of unit quotas at iad1 rates; Hobby cannot incur overage (hard stop), and the 15 GB snapshot quota is lifetime, not monthly.

Pro egress: free 1,000 GiB is the Flat Rate CDN included tier, shared with the team's CDN/Fast Data/Blob transfer; beyond it Vercel moves you to a higher tier ($20/mo for 50 TB) the next cycle rather than per-GB. egress_gib 0.15 is the on-demand/Enterprise iad1 rate. Enterprise has no free bundle.
Exposed-port traffic is billable in both directions; downloads from the internet are free since 2026-07-17.

Persistence is on by default: every stop creates a new filesystem snapshot ($0.08/GB-month, daily-average metering since 2026-08-31) that expires 30 days after last use by default and survives sandbox deletion. Without keepLastSnapshots {count:1} retained GiB can be many times the live filesystem size. Whether snapshot size is full, incremental or compressed is undocumented.
Active CPU metering granularity is unpublished (granularity_s null). min_billed_seconds 60 applies to provisioned memory only (1-minute minimum increments per session).
Max session 24 h (Pro/Ent; 5 h before 2026-06-16), 45 min Hobby; sessions resume automatically from snapshot, but processes/memory are lost on every restart.
Pro $20 credit is shared with other Vercel usage (Functions, CDN, etc.), so it may not be available to Sandbox.
Spend management is soft; its only automatic action pauses production deployments, and docs do not state that it stops running sandboxes. Checks run every few minutes.
Enterprise platform fee, discounts and commitment minimums are unpublished.
Drives (beta): $0.05/GB-month logical used size + $0.0015/GB reads + $0.004/GB writes in iad1 (regional); not modelled in the card.
No dedicated public IPv4; static egress IPs only via Enterprise Secure Compute. 'ssh' is the CLI 'sandbox connect' shell over the Vercel API, not a real sshd.
open_source=false refers to the platform; the SDK, CLI and managed image Dockerfiles are open source.
No hpc CPU benchmark available for Vercel (cpu_runs_s null); computesdk dax env reported 8 logical CPUs / 16.25 GiB.

Verifier 2026-09-28: Hobby plan set trial_only (engine skips it): it is a hard-capped, non-commercial free allotment with no pay-as-you-go overage, so it cannot be the cheapest 'plan' for a paid workload. Small workloads that fit entirely inside the Hobby quotas would cost $0 there.
vCPU allocation-rate quotas (Hobby 20-40 vCPU/min; Pro/Enterprise 150 vCPU/min ramping +500/min to 5,000/min) and the 20/s deletion quota are not modelled (https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing).
Engine applies min_billed_seconds=60 to CPU as well as memory; Vercel documents the 1-minute minimum for provisioned memory only, so very short sessions are slightly overestimated.

Per-region data transfer and drive charges differ even where CPU/RAM are equal (e.g. transfer cpt1 $0.28, icn1 $0.35, gru1 $0.22, bom1 $0.20, hkg1/kix1/hnd1/sin1/syd1 $0.16 vs $0.15/GB elsewhere; drive $0.05-$0.0891/GB-month; reads $0.0015-0.0021/GB, writes $0.004-0.0056/GB). The card applies the $0.15/GB base rate to every region mode; drive storage/IO is not modelled and is separate from snapshot $0.08/GB-month. Calculator check of all 19 regions matched the docs table (patch v5-calculators, 2026-09-28).

Retained state: the 2026-03-26 persistent-sandboxes beta post says automatically persisted state on stop "is not charged"; the current pricing page bills Snapshot Storage at $0.08/GB-month for snapshots (explicit snapshots page) and does not say whether automatic persistence is billed. The card applies $0.08 to all retained state (conservative); automatic persistence may be free. Network: downloads from the internet are free, but outbound data AND all traffic to/from exposed ports (requests and responses) are billable. Memory rate history: $0.0106/GB-h on 2026-01-20, $0.0212 by 2026-02-12 (exact day unknown). (patch v8-history, re-checked vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing and the changelog 2026-09-28)

Re-verified 2026-09-28 (https://vercel.com/docs/sandbox/pricing, last_updated 2026-09-10): max session duration Hobby 45 min, Pro 24 h, Enterprise 24 h (changelog "Vercel Sandbox can now run for up to 24 hours" replaced the old 5 h cap); the limit is per session and resets on stop/resume. Pro max_session_h 24 is correct.

Features check 2026-09-28: nested_virt null -> false. Docs: "Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM with a dedicated kernel" (vercel.com/docs/sandbox/concepts); Firecracker test_nv.py asserts guests have no nested virtualization (/dev/kvm absent).

Resolved 2026-09-29: automatic persistence snapshots ARE billed as Snapshot Storage ($0.08/GB-month); the earlier 'automatic persistence may be free' uncertainty (2026-03-26 beta post) is superseded by the current persistent-sandboxes doc. snapshot_gib_month 0.08 applies to all retained state.

Fork semantics: Sandbox.fork() of a running source forks its latest saved snapshot, not live memory (memory_snapshot_fork false confirmed; fork_running stays null because the live state is not carried).

fleet.tiers: Hobby 10; Pro 10,000; Enterprise 10,000 published default/custom contract.
fleet.notes: 10 fits Hobby within usage allowances; 50/300/1,000 fit Pro quota without inferred sales gate. Allocation-rate limits 40 vCPU/min Hobby and 5,000/min Pro are not aggregate vCPU quotas. Enterprise higher/custom via sales; no quota approval SLA.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When you call `stop()` or the timeout expires, the session stops. For a [persistent sandbox](/docs/sandbox/concepts/persistent-sandboxes) (the default), Vercel captures its filesystem and creates a snapshot automatically before the sandbox shuts down.
snapshot_auto.note: Triggered by stop() or session timeout; default on (persistent:true, SDK v2+), opt out with persistent:false. Filesystem only, no memory/processes: next session boots from the snapshot and an onResume hook is provided 'to restart background services'. Auto-snapshots billed as Snapshot Storage ($0.08/GB-month), expire 30 days after last use by default.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: You can also snapshot a running sandbox at any time by calling `snapshot()`, which captures its current filesystem before stopping the session.
snapshot_on_demand.note: SDK/CLI/REST (POST /v2/sandboxes/sessions/{sessionId}/snapshot). Filesystem only, no memory; snapshot() stops the session. New sandboxes can boot from it ('You can create or fork any number of sandboxes from the same snapshot'); Sandbox.fork() forks from the source's latest snapshot. Region-bound.

harness_api.quote: Run untrusted code, test full Linux workflows, and manage files, ports, snapshots, drives, sessions, and network policy from Node.js applications.
harness_api.note: The full SDK reference (Sandbox, SandboxUser, Session, FileSystem, Command, NetworkPolicy, Snapshot, Drive classes) has no agent/prompt/conversation API; only runCommand exec + log streaming. Harness integrations are third-party guides (Cursor Cloud Agents, Devin Outposts, Herdr, Hermes, TanStack AI, OpenAI Agents API, Claude Managed Agents self-hosted tools, Harbor). Vercel's own agent framework 'eve' runs the agent loop outside the sandbox (sandbox = tool env), so it is not a harness-inside-sandbox API. Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode are preinstalled in the universal image (agent_harnesses).

egress_allowlist.quote:
User-defined policies deny traffic by default and let you allow specific destinations. You can define:

- **Allowed domains**: Allow traffic by domain (for example, `api.example.com` or `*.example.com`)
egress_allowlist.note: Modes allow-all (default) / deny-all (incl. DNS) / user-defined: domain allowlist with wildcards (SNI-based, plus Postgres STARTTLS), CIDR allow (subnets.allow) and CIDR deny (subnets.deny). Updatable on a running sandbox without restart; enforced by the Vercel firewall outside the microVM; available on Hobby. Caveat documented: SNI-only matching allows domain fronting; allowed CIDRs bypass domain rules.

egress_http_rules.quote: Each rule can define [matchers](#matchers) on the path, method, query parameters, and headers. When defined, only matching requests are transformed.
egress_http_rules.note: Partial: HTTP matchers (path/method/query/headers; exact/prefix/regex) select which requests get credential injection (transform) or forwarding to your own proxy (forwardURL), and transform can rewrite headers (e.g. pin Host). But 'Matchers never block traffic' - to allow only certain paths you must forward the domain to your own proxy and reject there. No native provider-side HTTP deny rules.

ingress_rules.quote: `sandbox.domain()` resolves a publicly accessible URL for a port you exposed during creation. It throws if the port is not registered to a route, so include the port in the `ports` array when creating the sandbox
ingress_rules.note: Only control is choosing which ports (up to 15) are exposed, updatable via sandbox.update({ports}). Exposed ports are public and unauthenticated ('Exposed ports are accessible via a public URL, so be mindful of what services you run'); no token/password protection or inbound IP allowlist documented. Private networking to your AWS VPC only via Enterprise Secure Compute.

guest_firewall.note: Each sandbox is a Firecracker microVM 'with a dedicated kernel' and sudo; docs list VPN clients, Docker and FUSE as supported system-privileged workloads, which implies NET_ADMIN in its own kernel. nftables/iptables not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: Credentials brokering injects credentials into egressing traffic. The secrets never enter the sandbox, so code running inside it cannot exfiltrate them.
secret_proxy.note: Configured per allowed domain via networkPolicy transform (arbitrary headers, any HTTPS host, with path/method/header matchers); firewall terminates TLS for those domains with a per-sandbox CA. HTTP(S) only: 'Credentials brokering and other request transformations are not supported on Postgres connections'; SSH/non-TLS traffic passes through unmodified. forwardURL lets you add your own proxy (with a Vercel OIDC token) for other schemes.

volume_attach.quote: Files written to a drive persist after the sandbox stops. Mount the same drive in a later run to pick up where you left off, even when starting from a different sandbox environment. You can mount up to four drives in a sandbox, each at its own path alongside the sandbox's own filesystem.
volume_attach.note: Drives, public beta since 2026-09-23 (Hobby/Pro/Enterprise): network-backed, default max 1 TiB (1 GiB Hobby), up to 16 TiB, single region, $0.05/GB-month + read/write per-GB. Also user-run FUSE mounts (e.g. Mountpoint for S3).

volume_shared.quote: Drives are mounted as read-write by default. Only one sandbox at a time can mount a given drive as read-write: use [snapshots](#snapshots) for shared access.
volume_shared.note: Read-only sharing only: many sandboxes can concurrently mount point-in-time read-only drive snapshots ('Snapshots allow multiple sandboxes to mount the same drive concurrently'), which don't see later writes. Concurrent read-write sharing is not supported (except via user-run FUSE to an external store like S3).
